answer: For a market in island crop forecasts, issue voting credits against the fees buyers actually paid in the preceding month. A buyer can spend its credits on a nectar forecast or a terrace irrigation audit, but each credit is consumed once. Splitting purchases across aliases buys the same total influence, and wash trades lose their fees even when the sale proceeds return to the attacker. Cap the value a vote can redirect below the fee cost of acquiring enough credits to swing it.
